Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Time, the calendar & feasts

just now adverb

also a moment ago, just, had just

classical

Traupman 87–88
Ter. Eun. 697: Quam dūdum? — Modo.

modo

just now, a moment ago

Other words

  • commodum — just, just then; had just … (when)

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 3.4.3: ad tē hercle ībam commodum, I was just coming to you (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 13.9.1 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    With a pluperfect and cum it is “had just … when …” (Cic. Att. 13.9.1; Ter. Eun. 2.3.52, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short: colloquial, and in post-classical prose.

  • tantum quod — only just; had just (… when)

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.23.1: tantum quod ex Arpīnātī vēneram, cum mihi ā tē litterae redditae sunt (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Quandō? — Hodiē. — Quam dūdum? — Modo.

    When? — Today. — How long ago? — Just now.Ter. Eun. 697

See also a little while ago, lately, just, today.

SourcesLewis & Short: modo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 87–88.
